claims.text: Thermally activated short-range ordering forms in MoNbTaW during annealing.
Short-range ordering in annealed MoNbTaW produces atomic clustering.
Short-range ordering modifies dislocation mobility in MoNbTaW.
Short-range ordering modifies the phonon spectrum of MoNbTaW.
Changes in ordering, dislocation mobility, and phonon spectra produce measurable differences in yield strength and elastic moduli between annealed and quenched MoNbTaW.
Rapid quenching maintains a comparatively disordered atomic configuration in MoNbTaW.
Annealing MoNbTaW at 1200°C for 24–48 hours followed by controlled cooling promotes short-range ordering.
The governing structural mediator is the degree of short-range ordering, including atomic clustering and local lattice distortions.
Atom probe tomography, high-resolution TEM, and diffraction can quantitatively characterize the proposed short-range ordering.
Thermal energy during annealing enables constituent atoms to rearrange into short-range-ordered clusters.
Short-range-ordered clusters act as obstacles to dislocation motion.
Short-range-ordered clusters modify lattice vibrational modes.
Quenched MoNbTaW has a random atomic distribution with minimal short-range order.
Annealed MoNbTaW will have higher yield strength than quenched MoNbTaW because short-range order pins dislocations.
Annealed and quenched MoNbTaW will exhibit different elastic moduli, diffraction peak positions, and inelastic-scattering signatures.
The mechanical and thermoelastic differences between the two thermal treatments will vary with temperature.
The proposed behavior is applicable from 800°C to 1200°C under inert or vacuum conditions but may not extend to lower temperatures or oxidizing environments.
Grain size and solute segregation could confound attribution of mechanical and thermoelastic changes exclusively to short-range order.
